A: the NEW badge is squashed into a flat oval, which distorts it. It has also been pulled away from the jar and left floating between the body copy and the CTA. The jar has shrunk to a small secondary element, and the oversized Shop Now button competes with the headline. B keeps the original's composition intact: the badge stays round and sits with the jar, and the headline, copy and CTA follow a clear left-aligned order. Its only real flaw is that it is mostly a slightly widened copy, leaving some unused width on the right.

A: the quote mark floats far above the quote, 'hours.' is orphaned on its own line, the headline is undersized for a story format, and the CTA and logo are jammed under an oversized bottle while the backdrop circle is a cropped, detached blob in the corner. B: the quote fits on one line and the CTA has room to breathe, but the headline is still tiny and runs edge to edge, there is a large dead gap between the CTA and the logo, and the circle is again stranded in the corner instead of sitting behind the bottle.

A: the 'Pick your sound' eyebrow has dropped below the body copy. The 'Obsidian One, $349' label floats over a detached shadow ellipse, far from the headphones. The 'Obsidian Buds' label has turned into a fake pill next to the CTA, the earbuds have shrunk to an icon, and the headphones are small and jammed against the right edge. A: the six stats are split into fragments on both sides of the headline (40 h on the left, three stacked by the headphones, -38 dB and 6 mics on the far right). The legal line is the same size as the subtitle and sits in among the stats. The CTA hangs below and left of the headline instead of lining up with it, a cropped dark circle is left in the top-right corner, and the stat labels are too small to read. B is worse. The CTA is jammed against the left edge and touches the subtitle ('$349Every number…'). The subtitle and legal text run together as one long line, and 250 g and BT 5.4 float as tiny orphans above it. The large OBSIDIAN logo on the right competes with the headline, the remaining stats are illegibly small, and a cropped circle is left in the top-left corner.

A: the headline is shrunk to roughly 11px italic, so it has none of the weight it carries in the original. The cyan quote mark is a barely visible speck, and the 'Rated 5 out of 5' line is tiny. The text block also starts at an arbitrary x≈170, leaving a dead strip on the left and a big empty middle before the logo. B: it has the same undersized headline and speck-sized quote mark. On top of that, its four-line stack is jammed against the left edge (about 5px margin) and squeezed from top to bottom, with the rating line almost touching the bottom edge. That makes B more cramped and less intentional than A's slightly better-spaced block.

Both break the product pairing the same way: the serum bottle shrinks to a tiny sliver in the bottom-left corner, the peach circle becomes a stray cropped blob in the bottom-right, and the jar floats alone, so the 'duo' imagery is lost. In A, the centred logo doesn't match the left-aligned text, but the headline and body copy have proper spacing between them. B pushes a small logo into the top-right corner away from the left-aligned column, jams the body copy against the headline, and leaves a dead gap between the jar and the CTA, so it is slightly worse.

A keeps a sensible bottle-left / quote-right structure with readable quote and attribution, but the bottle is cropped at the top edge, the CTA pill is oversized and sits on the cropped peach circle, and the circle no longer backs the product, so the brand motif loses its meaning. B gets the reading order wrong: the CTA and logo sit at the top above the quote. The quote is set small, the bottle shrinks to a minor element, the circle drifts off on its own in the bottom right, and the lower half is mostly dead space.

A keeps the logo at top and has no collisions, but the cream jar is reduced to an unreadable speck stranded below the CTA, the bottle sits off-centre against a right-shifted circle, $48 is shrunk so it no longer dominates, the 'THE NIGHT SET' eyebrow has moved below its own copy, and there is a large dead gap above the button. B keeps a big $48, but the price and copy run across the circle's edge, the bottle overlaps the circle edge awkwardly, the logo is demoted to the bottom next to a tiny jar with an illegible label, and the eyebrow is again misordered below the body copy. Both are broken; A is slightly cleaner and keeps the brand in its original place.

Both break the reading order the same way: the CTA sits at the very top, above the message, the 'Clinically tested' eyebrow drops below the subhead, the product jar shrinks to a tiny footer thumbnail and the legal text is microscopic. A: the jar label is squashed and illegible and the centred CTA doesn't share the left edge used by the text. B is slightly worse: its headline breaks awkwardly ('in' / '28 days'), its CTA is indented off the headline's left edge, and it leaves a dead band between the image and the footer.

A keeps the 'Lumen & Fig' wordmark and fig mark dominant, but the circle is stretched into an oval and cropped at top, bottom and right, the wordmark straddles the oval's edge, and 'Skincare, slowly.' runs almost into the right canvas edge, so it can't ship. B has the hierarchy upside down: the tagline is larger than the shrunken brand name, the logo is jammed against the left edge and the fig mark sits on the oval's outline, and the circle is squashed into a wide ellipse, so the brand is lost.

A: the text panel runs off the top, right and bottom edges, so it reads as a cropped slab instead of the original floating card. The logo is indented and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge, the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow has dropped below the body copy, the right earcup touches the panel edge, and the centred CTA clashes with the left-aligned text. B: it keeps the floating card with a clean top margin and the logo aligns with the text, but the card still bleeds off the right edge. B also moves the eyebrow below the body copy, the earcup butts against the card, the logo is tiny, and the CTA is centred under left-aligned copy. B is the tidier of the two and closer to the original.

A has a clear left-to-right order (logo, headphones, headline, CTA), but the logo sits jammed against the top-left edge, the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow is cut off from the logo far below it, the subline is tiny, the oversized CTA runs right to the canvas edge, and the city background is gone. B is worse: the headphones are cropped off the left edge, and the logo, subline and eyebrow are crammed into one tiny bottom row in the wrong order, with the eyebrow trailing after the subline and the logo made trivial.

Both scramble the reading order the same way: the 'Obsidian One, $349' price floats above the 'PICK YOUR SOUND' eyebrow, which now sits below the body copy. In both, the earbuds shrink to a speck stranded beside the bottom logo, and the 'Obsidian Buds' label is cut off from its product. A collides the Compare Models button with the buds' plinth ellipse, but its two-line headline keeps a strong hierarchy. B avoids that collision but leaves an empty plinth floating as dead weight, shrinks the headline to one weaker line, and makes the call to action smaller, so it is marginally worse.

A: the headphones are cropped at the left edge, and the teal circle is cut off from the product and floats behind the right-hand stats column. The stats are reordered, and their labels are microscopic. The legal disclaimer sits beside the tagline at the same weight and wraps raggedly. Still, the headline, logo and CTA read as one clear block. B is far worse: the six stats are scattered around the canvas as tiny fragments (250 g crammed at the top edge, 6 mics floating top right). The legal text and the tagline are squeezed into narrow one-word-per-line columns. The CTA is a small pill lost at the bottom, and there is no grouping or grid at all.

A keeps the headline as the clear focal point, puts source and rating on one tidy line and anchors the logo at the right, which reads left to right. Its flaws: the text block starts about 160px in with nothing to its left, the quote mark has shrunk to a speck, and the logo is small and isolated far from the copy. B stacks four tight lines (quote mark, headline, source, rating) into the left half. Its headline is shrunk and the cyan source line is nearly as big as the headline, which flattens the hierarchy. The rating is tiny, and the right half of the banner is empty, so the layout is lopsided.

A: the CTA, NEW FLAVOUR and ZERO SUGAR row sits under the headline and shares its left edge, but the 'NEW FLAVOUR' badge is shrunk until it can't be read, there is a dead blue gap of about 150px on the left, and the yellow circle behind the logo is cut off at the right and bottom edges, so it reads as clutter jammed into the corner. B: the headline is larger, but the CTA and badge row is jammed against the bottom-left corner and doesn't line up with the headline. 'NEW FLAVOUR' is again unreadable, and the oversized FIZZBANG! logo pill competes with the headline and pushes the 'Grab a Can' button even further down the hierarchy, with the same clipped yellow circle.

A: '$3' sits above '2 FOR', so the offer reads backwards. The FIZZBANG logo shrinks to an unreadable pill and is jammed into a cramped bottom-left strip with a tiny CTA and tiny tagline, while a large dead area sits around the headline and the can is crowded against the right edge. B: it also reverses '$3'/'2 FOR', '$3' has shrunk so much it no longer dominates, and the CTA and logo pills are small and pressed under the tagline. But the tagline is readable, the logo is still legible, and the text block sits as one coherent group beside the can, so it is the less broken of the two.

A keeps the original's top-to-bottom order (logo, can, '2 FOR', '$3', copy, CTA) with clean centring and even spacing. Its only flaws are the orphaned 'long.' in the body copy and body text that's small at this width. B breaks the reading order: '$3' sits above '2 FOR', so the offer reads backwards. The '$3' presses against the left and top edges, and the FIZZBANG logo is shrunk into the bottom-left corner almost touching the edge, which badly demotes the brand.

A: the yellow date card, which is the key 'SAT 22 NOV, 8PM–1AM' info, has shrunk to an unreadable thumbnail in the top left. The 'FIZZBANG ARCADE NIGHT' eyebrow has dropped to the bottom below the body copy, the controller is a tiny afterthought, and the pattern block is a big generic crop. Still, the headline leads clearly and the CTA is prominent. B: the same unreadable date card, plus the body copy is squeezed into a tiny four-line ragged column jammed into the top-left corner beside the logo, which makes a cluttered, misaligned header. The headline is pushed below the pattern, and the eyebrow is tiny at the bottom. That makes B's hierarchy and reading order worse than A's.

A keeps a sensible order (headline, subcopy, controller, CTA), but the CTA is centred while the text is left-aligned, the Fizzbang can that was a hero item is shrunk to a tiny icon next to an undersized logo, and there is dead space below the CTA. B puts the CTA above the headline, so the reading order is backwards. Its button is also off the headline's left edge (it starts further right), there is a large unexplained gap between the headline and subcopy, and the can is again a tiny afterthought at the bottom left.

A keeps the headline and a readable yellow 'Pick Your Flavour' CTA, but breaks up the flavour list: 'Cola Crash' sits alone under the logo, 'Lime Zap' and 'Grape Pop' are tiny and jammed around the CTA, and the five items are out of order. B has a cleaner headline row, but its CTA is a tiny, illegible white pill under the logo. B also turns the remaining flavours into an unreadable micro-list on the right and shrinks the can to a sliver, so the call to action effectively disappears.

A: the white panel fills almost the whole strip, so the pop-art shapes shrink to slivers at the edges. The FIZZBANG! logo is jammed against the left canvas edge and spills onto a pink/blue fragment, and the CTA sits flush against the right edge with no margin. B keeps a recognisable pop-art block on the left (pink circle, dark quarter-circle, yellow stripe), which preserves the brand feel, and the headline and CTA have better breathing room. But B's logo sits on top of the busy yellow stripe and blue background, straddling the edge of the panel, and the right side ends in an unbalanced empty white area.

A: the headline is jammed against the top and left edges. 'Kiln Lane' runs straight into 'EXHIBITION' with no gap, the eyebrow label now sits after the address instead of above the title, and the date block is tiny with an unreadable hours line, though the image fills the right side sensibly. B: the image is pushed off the left edge, leaving a blank white strip about 110px wide, and 'Kiln LaneEXHIBITION' collides the same way. Its date box is also tiny with an illegible second line, and the logo is a speck, so the layout looks lopsided and unfinished.

A: the logo lockup is bigger than the quote, which flips the original order where the quote leads. Everything is packed into the upper two-thirds, so the bottom ~200px is dead space. The attribution and logo sit close together while a large gap is left above the quote. B: the logo is even larger and overpowers the small quote, again flipping the hierarchy, and the attribution is tiny and low-contrast. Still, B spreads its content down the full height, and its quote breaks onto two more even lines ('…quiet enough / to hear the light move'), so it reads as a more deliberate story layout.

A: the 'Plan a Visit' CTA sits at the very top above the logo and the 'NOW OPEN' eyebrow drops to the bottom, so the reading order is upside down. But 'NOW OPEN' sits below the body copy, oversized and tracked out so it competes with the headline. The logo floats mid-canvas cut off from the headline it should introduce, and the photo strip is a token sliver.

A: the watch case is cut off by the left canvas edge. The Monograph logo shrinks to a tiny mark next to the legal text, so the brand nearly disappears. The price is almost as large as the headline, so they compete for attention. Still, the headline, price, copy and CTA have clear spacing and a sensible left-to-right reading order. B: it has the same cropped watch and tiny, illegible logo, and it is worse because the headline runs into the 'Book a Fitting' button with almost no gap. The middle text block is cramped against both the watch and the CTA, and the legal text is squeezed under the copy.

A: the headline breaks badly, leaving 'warranty' alone on its own line. The logo shrinks to a tiny mark wedged beside the legal text, and the legal block is crammed against the bottom edge. The price now sits above the descriptive copy, and the oversized CTA crowds the text. B: the headline breaks cleanly ('Built to outlast / the warranty') and the vertical spacing is more even, but the logo is still a tiny, illegible mark buried next to the microscopic legal text, so the brand is lost. B shares A's price/copy reorder, and its legal text sits on the bottom edge.

A leaves a huge dead blue void between the subcopy and the CTA, reduces the ocean photo to an unreadable sliver at the bottom with a stray white line, and pushes the logo to the right while the text is left-aligned, so nothing shares an axis. B also cuts the photo down to thin strips at the top and bottom and centres the logo over left-aligned text, and its headline and copy sit tight to the edges, but the larger headline and evenly spaced stack fill the tall format with a clear headline-to-CTA reading order.

A: the suitcase is jammed against the left edge and looks clipped, the Book button sits right against the right edge, the Meridian logo is shrunk to an illegible speck tucked in the bottom-left with 'from' stranded beside it, and $199 now sits above 'New York', which flips the reading order. B: the suitcase is fully visible and the Book CTA is big with proper margins, but the logo wordmark collides with 'from' ('Meridian from' runs together), the logo is far too small to read, 'from' is separated from the price, and the $199/New York order is also flipped. Both are broken; B is less bad.

A: the three fare cards are shrunk to tiny scattered tiles with unreadable city names and 'from' labels, the logo is wedged between two cards, and the body copy is pushed off to the side of the CTA, but the card order and the headline-then-CTA flow survive. B is worse: the CTA sits at the top above everything, the cards are out of order (Reykjavik, Lisbon, Marrakech) and just as tiny, and the body copy appears above the headline it supports, so the reading order is jumbled and the layout doesn't read as designed.

A keeps a sensible reading order (logo → suitcase → headline → subcopy → CTA → legal), but the white circle has come loose from the suitcase and floats as a meaningless blob in the top-right. The left-aligned headline and subcopy clash with the centred logo, CTA and legal, and the legal block is a narrow, near-illegible column jammed under the button. B is worse: it puts the 'How It Works' CTA at the top-left before the headline, which breaks the reading order and the hierarchy. Its logo partly overlaps the stray circle, there's a large dead gap between the subcopy and the suitcase, the suitcase sits low and small, and the legal text runs as tiny full-width lines against the bottom edge.

A: the headline and logo panel are strong, but the fare list is broken. Berlin and Madrid have lost their prices, Rome is missing, the cities are out of order, the CTA pill runs over the blue panel edge, and the fine print sits mid-list and is clipped at the panel. B is worse: every price is gone, so the offer itself is lost. The city labels are tiny and scattered on both sides, Madrid and the fine print are dark text on blue and unreadable, and the blue panel stops short and leaves white strips.

A: the headphones are cropped at the left edge and clipped by the panel. The logo sits under the headline, so the brand reads after the message. The subline runs straight into the 'OBSIDIAN ONE' eyebrow with no gap, and both are tiny. B: the order logo → product → headline → CTA is clearer, but the logo and eyebrow are split into the top and bottom corners with dead space between them. The CTA is jammed against 'don't.', the headphones are shrunk to a small icon, and almost all of the city backdrop is lost.

A: '$3' sits above '2 FOR', so the offer reads backwards. There is dead space across the top and at the far right, and the text block is crowded against the bottom. B: it also reads '$3' then '2 FOR'. Worse, the CTA, the FIZZBANG logo and the 'Every flavour' copy are crushed into an illegible strip along the bottom-left edge; the logo is unreadable and the brand is effectively lost. A reads well left to right (logo, headline, CTA) and keeps a pop-art panel. But the panel is a cramped, cropped scrap (half a pink circle, a navy wedge), and the FIZZBANG pill straddles its edge over the yellow stripe, so the overlap looks accidental. B removes almost all of the brand graphics, leaving stray pink and blue slivers at both edges; its logo pill is jammed against the left canvas edge and the CTA nearly touches the right edge, so it has no margins and looks like a cropped strip rather than a designed banner.

A: the headline runs almost into the 'Book a Fitting' pill, which is jammed against the right edge. The watch is cut off at the left edge and the top/bottom, the Monograph logo has shrunk to an illegible speck beside the legal text, and the legal text is unreadable. However, the watch still bleeds off the top and bottom edges, the logo is still tiny and buried next to the fine print, and the legal text is too small to read, so it needs fixing before it can ship.

A: the Meridian logo has shrunk to an unreadable size and sits jammed against the orphaned word 'from', so the price reads as '$199 / New York' with the order of the original reversed; the suitcase sits off-centre with dead space around it, but the Book CTA is prominent and correctly placed. B has the same tiny, unreadable logo and 'from' fragment and the same reversed order, and is worse: the suitcase is cropped against the left and top canvas edges, and the Book button is undersized and pressed against the right edge, so the edge margins are broken.

A breaks the reading order. The CTA and logo sit at the top, the subhead floats above the headline, and the three price cards are shrunk to unreadable slivers scattered down a centre column out of order (Reykjavik, Lisbon, Marrakech), with large dead gaps between them. B keeps the cards in their original order and puts the CTA at the end, but the tiny cards with illegible city names are still scattered, the logo is sandwiched between two cards, and the subhead wraps badly beside the button and leaves 'way.' orphaned. A: the card fills almost the whole banner, so the leaf imagery is reduced to slivers. The bottle is jammed against the left edge and straddles the card border, an unintended collision. Its flaws: the headline almost touches the Shop the Serum button with no gutter, and the eyebrow and logo sit below the copy instead of above it, which inverts the original reading order.

A: the Lumen & Fig logo has shrunk to an illegible speck at the bottom of the card, so the brand is effectively lost. The 'NEW NIGHT SERUM' eyebrow sits below the body copy, so the reading order is wrong, and the bottle is cropped at the bottom with the card floating awkwardly. B: the logo stays readable and in proportion, but it has the same eyebrow-below-body order problem. Its card is jammed against the top, right and bottom canvas edges, and the bottle runs into the top edge and is cropped at the bottom, so the edges need margin fixes before it could ship.

A: the supporting copy, 'Worth $72' line and 'THE NIGHT SET' eyebrow are squeezed into one tiny, illegible strip along the bottom edge, with the jar shrunk to a speck in the middle of it. The serum bottle runs from the top edge off the bottom, and the circle is cut off behind the CTA, so only the logo, price and button are readable. B: the copy is readable and grouped under the price, but the eyebrow now sits last, below its own copy. The bottle is cut off at the bottom edge, the jar is an orphaned speck clipped at the bottom, and the CTA sits on top of a cropped fragment of the circle; it is weak but better than A.

A: the 'CLINICALLY TESTED' eyebrow has moved below the subcopy and been enlarged into a heavy line that competes with the headline. The legal block floats unreadably under the leaf panel, away from the copy column. The jar is cut off from the leaves and stranded bottom-left. The Lumen & Fig logo is blown up so large it rivals the headline. B: the eyebrow is also out of order, sitting below the subcopy. The right column is crammed (headline, subcopy, eyebrow, CTA, legal and logo stacked with almost no breathing room). The jar has shrunk to a near-invisible thumbnail, which loses the key product image. Still, B keeps a clearer headline-to-CTA hierarchy with a prominent button and a logo in proportion, so it is slightly less broken.

A: the logo sits between the '10 min' and '250 g' stats, and the Pre-order CTA is at the very top, above the headline. The six stats are scattered as fragments around the headphones ('40 h' and 'BT 5.4' are wedged into the tagline). The legal note is set as large as body copy. The dark teal circle is lost, so the reading order and grouping are wrecked. B: the stats are still scattered fragments, and '40 h', the tagline and 'BT 5.4' are crammed at the top over a cropped circle remnant. The logo is tiny, and the legal note is oversized, competing with the copy. But the headline → headphones → CTA order is roughly kept and the CTA is prominent near the bottom. A: the OBSIDIAN logo is shrunk to an unreadable sliver, so the brand is lost. The headline is oversized and crowds the logo. The Shop button is jammed against the right edge, leaving uneven margins and a lopsided balance. B: keeps the original's left-centre-right rhythm with a readable logo, a balanced headline and even margins. It only needs minor polish: the headline and Shop button are a little small for 320px, and the button's left gap is tight.

A: the FIZZBANG logo pill is oversized and clipped at the bottom and right edges. The CTA and both badges are tiny and unreadable under the headline, the can is a small sliver, the yellow circle is gone and the left 170px is empty. B: the yellow circle has become a cropped blob jammed into the top-left corner with the 'Grab a Can' CTA sitting on it. Both put '$3' above '2 FOR', so the offer reads backwards. A: the headline and subline are stacked sensibly with the CTA on the right, but the can is a tiny sliver with an illegible label, and the yellow circle has shrunk to a stray dot that collides with the corner of the Try It button. A reads left to right: the FIZZBANG! pill sits on the left and the SINCE 2026 badge on the right, both on one centre line. A has a sensible banner split (headline left, photo right in proportion), but the date block's 'Tuesday to Sunday' line is unreadably tiny, the 'EXHIBITION' kicker sits at the end of the address line instead of above the headline, and the logo has shrunk to an illegible speck, so the hierarchy below the headline falls apart. A: the logo and its tiny 'MONOGRAPH' wordmark sit on the grainy grey photo outside the white card, so the brand mark has poor contrast. A stacks everything under the watch: the CTA almost touches the legal block, which leaves a cramped bottom under an empty top. A: the Meridian logo is blown up as large as the headline and sits on the busy hill/sea crop, with its last letter jammed against the blue panel edge, so it competes with 'Lisbon from $89'; the subline is microscopic and unreadable at strip height. A: the Meridian logo sits on the photo and its wordmark runs across the photo/blue panel boundary. The photo is cropped to a meaningless green hill sliver, so the sea-and-sky imagery is lost. The subline is tiny and floats far below the headline. The oversized Book Now button competes with the headline and is jammed against the right edge. B: the headline and subline are tightly grouped and readable, which gives a clear left-to-right reading order. However, the logo is tiny and sits on a busy hill image, the photo crop still loses the original's open-sea feel, and the CTA nearly touches the right canvas edge.
